hero.title: Give AI agents useful tools.
hero.lede: Dekopon is a self-hosted agent harness with a separate permission broker. The model may request an action. The broker verifies who asked, applies policy and hard limits, then records what happened.

why.title: Do not make the model trusted. Limit what it can cause.
why.intro: A harness gives a model instructions, tools, and a loop. Dekopon adds a separate authority layer around those tools. Useful exploration stays possible without turning model text into operating-system permission.

cards.title: Untrusted content can steer a model.
cards.body: Messages, webpages, issues, pull requests, tool results, and the model’s own output can all contain misleading instructions. Dekopon treats every resulting tool request as an untrusted proposal.

cards.title: A general shell can carry ambient authority.
cards.body: Host files, inherited environment variables, subprocesses, and unrestricted sockets turn one mistake into a machine-wide problem. Dekopon’s shell has none of those by default.

cards.title: Permission should survive the prompt.
cards.body: Identity, policy, credentials, execution limits, and audit live outside the model session. A persuasive string cannot claim a principal, widen a host list, or invent a missing capability.

why.bridge: The practical goal is containment: narrow, attributable, reviewable, and revocable authority around an untrusted model.

journey.title: Alice may comment. Merge stays absent.
journey.intro: This synthetic pull-request agent shows the whole security story without starting from YAML or Rust types.

steps.label: Identify
steps.title: Slack authenticates Alice.
steps.body: The gateway carries a canonical Slack subject. The message cannot name its own trusted principal.

steps.label: Propose
steps.title: The model asks to comment.
steps.body: Its one sandboxed tool resolves a familiar gh command into one narrow capability request.

steps.label: Decide
steps.title: The broker checks every boundary.
steps.body: Cedar decides whether Alice may use this action through this agent. Separate constraints bind host, methods, calls, bytes, timeout, and credential.

steps.label: Execute
steps.title: One fresh provider call runs.
steps.body: A fresh Wasm store receives only approved host interfaces. Native broker HTTP injects the token after guest headers are checked.

steps.label: Record
steps.title: Decision and outcome remain linked.
steps.body: Hash-linked audit records the trusted identity, policy decision, constraints, outcome, and digest evidence without storing prompt or response bodies.
steps.detail: invocation ID + trace ID + policy digest

journey.denied: Still denied: approve, merge, arbitrary GitHub API, host shell

security.title: What the boundary changes—and what it does not.
security.intro: Dekopon names the safeguard and its limit. It does not claim to make models trustworthy, stop prompt injection, or turn a pre-production local deployment into a hardened multi-tenant service.

rows.threat: Prompt injection or a model mistake
rows.control: Model output can propose only named capabilities. The broker authorizes each call from fresh trusted context.
rows.limit: Dekopon does not detect prompt injection. Persistent history can make injected text last longer.

rows.control: Provider credentials stay out of prompts, shell state, and Wasm guests. Native HTTP injects a destination-bound value.
rows.limit: A permitted remote endpoint could still reflect the credential. Scope and trust that endpoint separately.

rows.control: No operating-system bash, inherited environment, host files, processes, or ambient sockets. Hosts, methods, calls, bytes, and time are bounded.
rows.limit: A compromised host or malicious process inside the current Unix UID trust domain remains out of scope.

rows.control: Chat identity comes from authenticated transport and owner-controlled broker mapping, never message text or provider input.
rows.limit: The local development subject is explicitly opt-in and is not authenticated by an external service.

rows.control: Decision, policy digest, execution outcome, evidence digest, invocation ID, and trace ID remain correlated.
rows.limit: The local audit checkpoint has no independent remote or signed anchor and cannot roll back an external effect.

limits: One local Unix UID is currently one trust domain
No independent audit anchor or incident-response automation

useCases.title: Give the same harness very different skills.
useCases.intro: Providers are independently released Wasm components. Each exposes narrow operations instead of handing the model a general plugin or operating-system process.

broker.title: The broker YAML makes every limit visible.
broker.intro: The story above becomes owner-authored configuration. This trimmed synthetic example names Alice, one provider operation, one credential, one destination, two methods, two calls, byte ceilings, and a timeout before the agent starts.
broker.yaml:
apiVersion: dekopon.dev/brokerd/v1alpha1
brokerPrincipal: local-broker
policyRevision: pr-commenter-2026-08
policiesPath: ./policies.cedar
credentialsPath: ./broker-credentials.yaml
providers:
  - ./gh-provider.wasm

identities:
  - uid: 65532
    principal: chat-gateway
    actor: { type: service, principal: chat-gateway }
    attestor:
      namespaces: [slack.example]
      chatScopes:
        - breadth: transportWide
          kind: slack
          transport: workspace-slack
identityMappings:
  - subject: slack.example.u123
    principal: alice

constraintSets:
  gh.pull-request.comment:
    provider: gh
    effect: external-write
    risk: Medium
    idempotency: conditional
    credential: github-comment-token
    constraints:
      timeoutMs: 15000
      maxOutputBytes: 8192
      http:
        allowedHosts: [api.github.com]
        allowedMethods: [GET, POST]
        maxRequests: 2
        maxRequestBytes: 16384
        maxResponseBytes: 262144
        allowPlaintextLoopback: false

authority.title: Alice may leave a comment.
authority.intro: In this synthetic deployment, Slack subject slack.example.u123 maps to principal alice. She may drive pr-commenter through chat-gateway, then request one GitHub comment capability.
authority.decisionBody: The rule matches trusted identity and routing context. It never reads Alice’s message or the provider input.
authority.constraintsTitle: The broker then applies the YAML envelope
authority.denial: Route Alice to release-bot and Cedar denies agent.prompt before any model call: the Agent resource no longer matches.

invariants.title: Text cannot become Alice
invariants.body: The principal comes from gateway attestation and broker mapping, never the prompt.

invariants.title: Prompt is a separate grant
invariants.body: Permission to drive pr-commenter does not imply permission to use its GitHub capability.

invariants.title: Comment is not merge
invariants.body: Each capability is a distinct Cedar action. Missing actions stay denied.

invariants.title: Policy cannot widen I/O
invariants.body: Cedar can allow the action. It cannot add hosts, methods, calls, time, bytes, or credentials.

execution.title: Use the shell training models already have.
execution.intro: Models already know variables, functions, pipelines, structured filters, conditionals, loops, exit codes, and defensive shell options. Dekopon keeps that exploration pattern inside a language with no host processes, files, environment, or ambient sockets.
execution.script:
set -euo pipefail
issue=$(tickets issue show T-42)
echo "$issue" | jq '{title, owner, state}'

for id in $(tickets issue list --state open | jq -r '.[].id'); do
  tickets issue show "$id" | jq '{id, owner, state}'
done
execution.result: one script · bounded JSON · explicit exit codes

cards.title: The training transfers
cards.body: Variables, loops, functions, pipes, command substitution, jq, getopts, read, and exit codes feel like shell transcripts frontier models already know.

cards.title: Providers become verbs
cards.body: A provider may declare a command word. Its pure resolver turns argv into one typed capability proposal.

cards.title: A command grants nothing
cards.body: Resolving tickets issue show does not authorize it. The same Cedar decision and broker constraints still run.

cards.title: Every loop has a ceiling
cards.body: Script steps, recursion, output, deadline, model turns, tool calls, provider fuel, memory, and broker I/O are all bounded.
